items.definition:
a Japanese poem of seventeen syllables, in three lines of five, seven, and five
She wrote a beautiful haiku about nature.

a small axe with a short handle
He used a hatchet to chop the small branches.

a homeless person, typically one who travels in search of work
The old hobo warmed himself by the fire.

a small group of people or things crowded close together
The players formed a huddle to discuss their strategy.

a style of lively dance or music; deceptive or glib talk
They were dancing to some cool jive music.

a girl or young woman
The bonnie lass sang a beautiful song.

a person who has won a medal in a competition or event
The gold medallist stood proudly on the podium.

A very small arachnid; a very small amount or degree.
The old book was infested with dust mites.

A place where bodies are kept, especially to be identified or examined.
The police took the body to the morgue for an autopsy.

(In golf) an extra stroke allowed after a poor shot, without penalty; a second chance to do something.
I hit a terrible shot, so I'll take a mulligan.

A puppet of the type created by Jim Henson; (informal) a foolish or incompetent person.
He felt like a muppet after making such a silly mistake.

A short novel or a long short story.
Ernest Hemingway's 'The Old Man and the Sea' is a famous novella.

A hydrocarbon of the alkane series, found in petroleum. Used to describe the anti-knock properties of fuel.
This car requires high-octane fuel.

A series of eight notes occupying the interval between two notes, one having twice or half the frequency of the other.
She sang the high note an octave above the melody.

The quality of being prudent; cautiousness.
He acted with prudence when making the difficult decision.

the time during which a program is running or a process is active
The software crashed during runtime.

a person who copies out documents, especially one employed to do this before printing was invented
In ancient times, a scribe was a highly respected profession.

a soldier stationed to keep guard or to control access to a place
The sentry stood guard at the gate all night.

the status of being a state
Alaska achieved statehood in 1959.

the small piece of something that is left after the main part has been used or broken off
He kept the ticket stub as a souvenir.

a secondary or subordinate group within a larger group
The research focused on a specific subgroup of the population.

skill and sensitivity in dealing with others or with difficult issues
He handled the delicate situation with great tact.

a vast, flat, treeless Arctic region
The polar bear roams across the vast tundra.

a loose-fitting garment
Ancient Romans often wore a simple tunic.

a small marine fish
We had fried whiting for dinner.

the first letter of the NATO phonetic alphabet
The pilot spelled out the word 'Alfa' over the radio.

a high mountain
They hiked through the rugged alp terrain.

a place where a battle is fought; a disputed area
The city became a battleground during the war.

a deep, loud roar
The lion's bellow echoed through the valley.

a shapeless mass or drop
A blob of paint fell onto the floor.

water saturated with salt
The pickles were preserved in a strong brine.

a person who draws cartoons
The cartoonist drew a funny caricature of the politician.

a person of mixed European and black descent; a language formed from a pidgin
Haitian Creole is spoken by most people in Haiti.

the action of being rescued or set free
They prayed for deliverance from their suffering.

the action of making something weaker or less concentrated
The dilution of the chemical reduced its toxicity.

a skin condition causing dry, itchy patches
She has suffered from eczema since childhood.

the action of forcing or throwing something out
The ejection of the player from the game caused a stir.

a substance that produces an electrically conducting solution when dissolved in a polar solvent
Sports drinks contain electrolytes to help rehydrate the body.

a fault or weakness
Patience was his greatest failing.

a secure position from which to advance
The company is trying to gain a foothold in the new market.

a defensive wall or other reinforcement built to strengthen a place against attack
The ancient city was protected by strong fortifications.

hairline
He noticed a slight receding of his hairline.

heiress
She was the sole heiress to a vast fortune.

holster
The police officer kept his pistol in a leather holster.

hunch (a feeling or guess)
I have a hunch that he's hiding something.

infographic
The company used an infographic to explain their new product.

innovator
Steve Jobs was a renowned innovator in the tech industry.

koi (fish)
Beautiful koi fish swam gracefully in the pond.

landfall
The hurricane is expected to make landfall early tomorrow morning.

layoff
The company announced a mass layoff due to financial difficulties.

limerick (a type of poem)
He wrote a funny limerick about a cat.

loner
He was always a bit of a loner, preferring his own company.

an important, powerful person
He became a media mogul after years of hard work.

a person who has no fixed home and moves from place to place
The tribe lived as nomads, following the herds.

a person who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable
He was a committed pacifist and refused to join the army.

A tall, fast-growing tree of the willow family.
The poplar trees lined the riverbank.

A person whose job is to generate and manage publicity for a public figure, a product, or a work of art.
The celebrity hired a publicist to manage her image.

A mischievous or cheeky person, especially a child or man.
The little rascal was always getting into trouble.

A person who takes part in a riot.
The police arrested several rioters after the protest.

The part of the leg between the knee and the ankle; a long, thin, flat piece of metal or other material.
He felt a pain in his shank after the long run.

A short, often boxed, article in a newspaper or magazine, presented alongside a main article and containing additional or explanatory material.
The newspaper article included a sidebar with statistics.

A person inclined to question or doubt all accepted opinions.
He was a skeptic about the new health claims.

A ship propelled by a steam engine.
The old steamship sailed across the ocean.

the occupation of land or property as a tenant
The tenancy agreement specifies the duration of the lease.
